Rashi on Shabbat 153a:11:1.english: One for whom night fell. He gives his pouch to a gentile - While it is still day.

Rashi on Shabbat 153a:11:2.hebrew: ואם אין עמו - הא יש עמו, לנכרי עדיף, כדמפרש בגמרא:
Rashi on Shabbat 153a:11:2.english: And if there is no [gentile] with him - [This implies that] if there is [one] with him, [giving it] to a gentile is preferable, as is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Shabbat 153a:11:3.hebrew: לחצר החיצונה - של עיר, שהוא מקום המשתמר ראשון, ובא לפרק מן החמור:
Rashi on Shabbat 153a:11:3.english: To the outer courtyard - of a city, which is the first guarded place, and he comes to unload from the donkey.

Rashi on Shabbat 153a:11:4.hebrew: נוטל - בידו מעליו כלים הניטלין בשבת, ושאין ניטלין — מתיר החבלים של אוכף שהן קשורים בהן, והשקין נופלין:
Rashi on Shabbat 153a:11:4.english: He takes - with his hand from off it [the donkey] vessels that may be moved on Shabbat; and [for those] that may not be moved, he unties the ropes of the saddle to which they are tied, and the sacks fall.

Rashi on Shabbat 153a:12:1.english: What is the reason it is permitted for him to give [it] to a gentile - And behold, he [the gentile] is his agent to carry it on Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 153a:12:2.english: Restrain himself - from saving his money.

Rashi on Shabbat 153a:13:1.hebrew: דוקא כיסו - דכיון דטרח בה, שע"י טורח הוא משתכר, חייס עלה, ואי לא שרית ליה הא, אתי לאיתויי:
Rashi on Shabbat 153a:13:1.english: Specifically his pouch - Since he toiled for it, as through toil he earns [it], he cares about it, and if you do not permit him this, he will come to carry [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 153a:13:2.hebrew: ולא אמרן - דמציאה לא, אלא דלא אתיא לידה קודם שתחשך ולא הגביהה ולא זכה בה:
Rashi on Shabbat 153a:13:2.english: And we only said - that [a] lost object [is] not [permitted], [only] where it did not come into his hand before dark, and he neither lifted it nor acquired it.

Rashi on Shabbat 153a:16:1.english: This [one is] a person - And there are [others] of his kind who are obligated in mitzvot, and it might come to be confused.

Rashi on Shabbat 153a:16:2.hebrew: לשוטה - יהיב, דלית ליה דעת כלל, אבל חרש דעתא קלישתא אית ליה, כדאמרי' ביבמות (דף קיג.):
Rashi on Shabbat 153a:16:2.english: To the imbecile - He gives [it to him], for he has no understanding at all; whereas a deaf-mute has a weak understanding, as we say in Yevamot (113a).

Rashi on Shabbat 153a:2:1.hebrew: אם בן עוה"ב הוא - שאם כשר היה, הכל בוכין עליו ומורידין דמעות ומספרים שבחו:
Rashi on Shabbat 153a:2:1.english: Whether he is a son of the World-to-Come - For if he was worthy, everyone weeps over him, sheds tears, and recounts his praise.

Rashi on Shabbat 153a:2:2.hebrew: אחים בהספידא דהתם קאימנא - בשעת מיתתי, התאמץ בהספד שלי שיתחממו ויכמרו רחמי העומדים ויבכו:
Rashi on Shabbat 153a:2:2.english: Stir [the hearts] during the eulogy, for I will be standing there - At the time of my death, exert yourself in my eulogy, so that the compassion of those standing [there] will be warmed and stirred, and they will weep.

Rashi on Shabbat 153a:2:3.hebrew: דהתם קאימנא - בשעת הספד, ואשמע איך תתחמם. אלמא, איצטריך לרב לאזהוריה אהספדא; וכיון דרב גברא רבה ובן העולם הבא, למה ליה לאזהוריה? הא אמר "מהספידו ניכר":
Rashi on Shabbat 153a:2:3.english: For I will be standing there - at the time of [my] eulogy, and I will hear how you grow fervent [in eulogizing]. Thus, Rav needed to instruct him regarding [his] eulogy; and since Rav [was] a great man and [worthy of] the World-to-Come, why did he need to instruct him? Behold, he said, "From his eulogy it is apparent."

Rashi on Shabbat 153a:2:4.hebrew: הא דמחממי ליה - להספידא, ואחים כו'. לעולם חמומי בעי, שאין בני אדם נכמרים כל כך על זקן. ומיהו, לאדם חסיד — כי מחממו בהספידא, מחממי ובכו כולהו; ולמי שאינו חסיד כל כך — מחממו ליה, ולא מחממו:
Rashi on Shabbat 153a:2:4.english: This [is a case] where they stir it up - [i.e.,] the eulogy, "and it is stirred, etc." [Indeed,] it always requires stirring up, for people are not so moved [with grief] over an old man. However, for a pious person, when they stir up [emotion] at the eulogy, they are stirred and all of them weep; whereas for one who is not so pious, they [try to] stir them up, but they are not stirred.

Rashi on Shabbat 153a:3:1.hebrew: דסנו ליה כולהו פומבדיתאי - משום דמוכח להו במילי דשמיא, ובני פומבדיתאי רמאין הן, כדאמרינן בשחיטת חולין (חולין קכז.): "פומבדיתאי לוייך, שני אושפיזך":
Rashi on Shabbat 153a:3:1.english: Whom all the Pumbeditans hate - Because he rebukes them in heavenly matters, and the people of Pumbedita are deceivers, as we say in Shechitat Chullin (Chullin 127a): "[If] a Pumbeditan accompanies you, change your lodging."

Rashi on Shabbat 153a:4:1.hebrew: ואזניך תשמענה דבר מאחריך לאמר זה הדרך לכו בה - מאחרי מטתך כשתמות תשמע, כשיאמרו: "זה הדרך שהלך בה זה, לכו בה" — מובטח שהוא בן העוה"ב:
Rashi on Shabbat 153a:4:1.english: And your ears shall hear a word behind you, saying: This is the path, walk on it - Behind your bier, when you die, you will hear [this] when they say: "This is the path that this [person] walked on, walk on it" — [one who receives such a eulogy] is assured that he has a share in the World-to-Come.

Rashi on Shabbat 153a:4:2.english: [Is] pleased with him - Their minds are at ease with them from what they hear about him and see in him.

Rashi on Shabbat 153a:4:3.english: Do things - That they will say in front of your bier at your eulogy.

Rashi on Shabbat 153a:4:4.hebrew: לאחר מטתך - היא היא, אלא שבגליל היו הספדנין לפני המטה וביהודה לאחר המטה:
Rashi on Shabbat 153a:4:4.english: Behind your bier - It is the same [thing], except that in the Galilee the eulogizers were in front of the bier and in Judea behind the bier.

Rashi on Shabbat 153a:5:1.hebrew: וכ"ש - שמפני שאינו יודע איזה יום ימות, וטובה תשובה יום אחד לפני מיתתו, נמצא כל ימיו בתשובה יהיו:
Rashi on Shabbat 153a:5:1.english: And all the more so - For since he does not know which day he will die, and repentance one day before his death is good, it follows that all his days will be [spent] in repentance.

Rashi on Shabbat 153a:5:2.english: Your clothes [should be] white - Your soul [should be] pure and clean.

Rashi on Shabbat 153a:6:1.hebrew: כלום חסר בית המלך - בתמיה. הכל מוכן, ושמא יבהילנו לבא פתאום, ואנו צריכין ליכנס לסעודה מקושטין:
Rashi on Shabbat 153a:6:1.english: Is the king's house missing anything - [Asked] as a rhetorical question. Everything is ready, and perhaps he will hurry us to come suddenly, and we must enter the feast adorned.

Rashi on Shabbat 153a:6:2.hebrew: כלום יש סעודה בלא טורח - עדיין יצטרכו לטרוח לצורכי סעודה של בית המלך, ויש לנו שהות הרבה להתקשט:
Rashi on Shabbat 153a:6:2.english: Is there a feast without toil? - They will still need to toil for the needs of the feast of the king's house, and we have plenty of time to adorn ourselves.

Rashi on Shabbat 153a:7:1.hebrew: יעמדו ויראו - ואף לעוה"ב, צדיקים יושבים ואוכלים, ורשעים עומדים ורואים:
Rashi on Shabbat 153a:7:1.english: Shall stand and watch - And so too in the World to Come, the righteous sit and eat, and the wicked stand and watch.

Rashi on Shabbat 153a:8:1.hebrew: ר"מ אומר - אין עומדין ורואין, שא"כ אף הם היו נראים מן הקרואים ולשמש, שכן דרך המשרתים עומדים, ואין כאן בושה:
Rashi on Shabbat 153a:8:1.english: Rabbi Meir says - They do not stand and watch, for if so, they too would appear [to be] among the invited guests and [there] to serve, since such is the way of the attendants [who] stand, and there is no shame here.

Rashi on Shabbat 153a:9:1.english: This is tzitzit - For the garment is whitened [by it].

Rashi on Shabbat 153a:9:2.hebrew: אלו תפילין - שהם שם משמן טוב, דכתיב: "וראו כל עמי הארץ כי שם וגו'", ותנא ר"א הגדול אומר: "אלו תפילין שבראש" (ברכות דף ו.):
Rashi on Shabbat 153a:9:2.english: These are phylacteries - For they are [referred to as] a "name," [likened to] good oil, as it is written: "And all the peoples of the earth shall see that the name [of the Lord is called upon you,] etc.," and it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer the Great says: "These are the phylacteries on the head" (Berakhot 6a).

Tosafot on Shabbat 153a:11:1.hebrew: מי שהחשיך כו' חרש שוטה וקטן - אע"ג דאמר לעיל בפרק כל כתבי (שבת דף קכא.) גבי קטן שבא לכבות דקטן העושה לדעת אביו אסור, מיהו הכא לא מיירי כגון דעביד הקטן עקירה והנחה, אלא כדאמרינן לקמן גבי חמור: כשהיא מהלכת מניחו עליה, וכשהיא עומדת נוטל הימנה. מ"ר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 153a:11:1.english: "One for whom night fell," etc., "a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor" - Even though [the Gemara] says earlier in the chapter Kol Kitvei (Shabbat 121a), regarding a minor who comes to extinguish [a fire], that a minor acting with his father's consent is forbidden, nevertheless here it is not speaking of a case where the minor performs lifting and placing, rather [it is] as we say below regarding a donkey: when it is walking he places [the pouch] upon it, and when it is standing he takes [it] from it. [From my teacher.]

Tosafot on Shabbat 153a:1:1.hebrew: ונשמתו עולה ושוב אינה יורדת - אף על פי כן, כשהיא רוצה היא יורדת, כי ההיא דלעיל דרבי אחי בר יאשיה, וכההיא מעשה דר' בנאה דחזקת הבתים (ב"ב דף נח. ושם), דהוה מציין מערתא; כי מטא למערתא דאברהם אבינו, אשכחיה לאליעזר עבד אברהם דקאי אבבא. אמר ליה: "מאי קא עביד אברהם?" כו', אמר ליה: "ניעול וניתי" כו' — אע"פ שנשמתו היתה גנוזה מתחת כסא הכבוד. מ"ר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 153a:1:1.english: And his soul ascends and does not descend anymore - Nevertheless, when it wishes, it descends, like that [incident] above of Rabbi Achi bar Yoshiyah, and like that incident of Rabbi Bana'ah in [the chapter] Chezkat HaBatim (Bava Batra 58a, and there [in the commentary]), who was marking [burial] caves; when he reached the cave of Abraham our forefather, he found Eliezer, the servant of Abraham, standing at the entrance. [Rabbi Bana'ah] said to him: "What is Abraham doing?" etc.; [Abraham] said to him [Eliezer]: "Let him enter and come [in]," etc. — even though his soul was stored away beneath the Throne of Glory. [From] my teacher, my master:
